text:
irene: Heads up: noticed clients on older SDKs keep hammering reconnects even after we send control/backoff events. Seems many SDKs ignore control events without an ack path.
matt: Confirmed. Dashboard shows t-777 reconnect attempts spike for 90s after a quota hump. Control events emitted but no client-side backoff observed.
oliver: Quick log snippet:
```
[15:21:10] proxy: emit control {"type":"backoff","backoff_ms":2000}
[15:21:11] client-js:v1 reconnect attempt -> resume_token=rt-42
[15:21:11] proxy: resume accepted (optimistic)
[15:21:11] runtime: quota fail -> 429
```
zara: The root cause is twofold: 1) control schema lacked a version field, 2) older SDKs silently ignore unknown in-stream events. We need a migration-safe control event format and a small ack handshake so proxy can know if a client understood the control.
irene: Proposal: add control_event_version and require clients to send a lightweight ack frame `{\"event\":\"control_ack\",\"nonce\":\"n-xxx\",\"ver\":2}` when they process a control event. Proxy then suppresses resume accept for non-acking clients for ~N ms or treats them as legacy and applies conservative rate limits.
matt: Also suggest `control_min_client_ver` in the control payload so we can gate behavior: `{\"type\":\"backoff\",\"backoff_ms\":2000,\"ver\":2,\"min_client_ver\":2}`. SDKs <2 will not ack and proxy will fallback to header-based TTL or hard throttle.
oliver: We should also avoid introducing blocking changes for unknown clients. Migration plan: send both v1 (legacy) and v2 (namespaced) control events for 2 weeks during canary. Example SSE stream (dual emit):
```
event: control
data: {"type":"backoff","backoff_ms":2000}

event: control.v2
data: {"type":"backoff","backoff_ms":2000,"ver":2,"nonce":"n-123","min_client_ver":2}
```
zara: For WS, send two frames back-to-back: first oldframe, then namespaced `control.v2`. Require v2 SDKs to ack by sending `control_ack`. If ack missing within 150ms, treat client as legacy.
irene: Telemetry: add metrics `control_event_sent.v2`, `control_ack_received.v2`, `control_unacked_clients`, `legacy_client_reconnect_rate` and tie to tenant tags. Add an alert if `control_unacked_clients` > 5% for >60s.
matt: Console UX: add a banner when a tenant has a high fraction of legacy clients and offer a one-click mitigation to enforce server-side conservative throttling or to display a migration guide for customers.
oliver: SDK changes: v2 SDKs will auto-ack control events and expose a `onControl` hook. Also add opt-out config for apps that intentionally ignore server backoff (for low-latency use cases).
zara: Security note: validate control_ack nonces; don't accept arbitrary acks. Nonces should be short-lived and unpredictable.
irene: Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: emit dual events in Canary 10% for 48h, collect `control_ack_received.v2` stats.
- Stage 2: send deprecation notice to customers, add console banner for tenants with many legacy clients.
- Stage 3: after 2 weeks, flip to only v2 for new connections and keep legacy handling for existing connections for 30 days.
ops-bot: Alert: t-777 legacy_client_reconnect_rate at 15:21 exceeded threshold.
deploy-bot: Canary: control-protocol v2 -> 10% (2026-03-13T15:20Z).
irene: Action items:
- matt: add telemetry + dashboard panels (PR)
- oliver: implement dual-emit in proxy + nonce generator + ack matching (PR)
- zara: SDK v2 spec + sample ack code + migration docs (PR)
- ops: add alert for control_unacked_clients and mitigation playbook (ticket)
- ui: console banner mock + tenant migration UX (figma link)
Please paste PR/ticket links here once created. Small sync tomorrow 11:00 to confirm canary gating. :white_check_mark:
